description:
Move the blocked-transition and startup-envelope cases that only the exit-code suite tests into the error-envelope suites.

## Background

`crates/jit/tests/cli_issue/exit_code_tests.rs` (39 subprocess tests) re-proves projected exit codes and also owns behaviour no other test owns. The exit-code projection suite owns command-to-exit-code bindings and their human/machine parity: outside it, a subprocess test asserts success or failure and the property it adds, and names a numeric exit code only for a command and code pair the projection has no row for. This entry covers these cases:

- `:312` and `:405`: a transition blocked by gates, human and JSON. They assert the `BLOCKED` details (`requested_state`, `actual_state`, gate blockers) and remediation commands (`gate evaluate`, `gate status-all`, `gate status --all`).
- `:493` and `:559`: a transition blocked by dependencies, JSON and human remediation text.
- `:605`: a missing dependency, whose blocker state is `missing`.
- `:1488`, `:1512` and `:1528`: startup envelopes. Repository-not-found emits `REPOSITORY_NOT_FOUND` under `--json` and empty stdout without it; a format that is too new emits `REPOSITORY_FORMAT_TOO_NEW`.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: Each case listed in the Background has an owning test with the same non-exit assertions. The blocked transitions live in `cli_issue/error_json_tests.rs` and the startup envelopes in `cli_issue/top_level_failure_envelope_tests.rs`.
- [hard] REQ-02: A moved case names a numeric exit code only where the projection has no row for its command and code.
- [hard] REQ-03: A behaviour an existing test in those files already owns is not duplicated.
title: Blocked-transition and startup envelope cases move beside their owners
